subtype: Clapping and snapping in peer groups [Expressing]
passage: At the open mic Farida snapped her fingers fast and clapped hard when her friend finished a poem, and half the room joined in. I was standing beside her. Later, when the teacher announced extra homework, Farida clapped slowly, one, two, three, with her eyebrows up. Some laughed. One boy said, "That was rude," but it seemed like a joke to me. I can't tell you what she felt inside, perhaps annoyed, perhaps just playing. The two claps looked nothing alike, though. The fast one made her friend beam. The slow one made the teacher raise an eyebrow back. I'm Deepika, and I was watching both.

qa.q: What did Farida do with her fingers when her friend finished the poem?
qa.a: She snapped her fingers fast and clapped hard.

qa.q: What might Farida have been feeling with her slow clap, and what else could it have been?
qa.a: She was probably annoyed at the extra homework and being dramatic, since she clapped slowly with her eyebrows up. Deepika admits it could just have been play.

qa.q: How could Farida avoid the slow clap being taken as mockery?
qa.a: She could smile, or add a few words to show it's a joke, and save slow claps for jokes among friends. Tone and speed carry the message.

qa.q: How did the friend read the fast clapping?
qa.a: The friend beamed, taking the fast snapping and clapping as praise. The teacher read the slow one differently and raised an eyebrow.

grounding: A teenager claps and snaps as approval among friends, and slowly claps sarcastically, and tone and speed show the difference.

subtype: Clapping and snapping in peer groups [Expressing]
passage:
Monday: Salma jumped up and clapped fast, snapping her fingers, as soon as Elizabeth finished her speech. Elizabeth grinned and went pink.
Thursday: Elizabeth ran in ten minutes late. Salma clapped slowly, one, two, three, and said, "Wow, welcome." Elizabeth's smile went stiff and she sat down without a word.
Saturday: Elizabeth said, "That slow clap felt like a jab." Salma blinked. "I meant it as a joke. Sorry, I'd better just say 'hey, you're here' next time." Elizabeth said, "Yes, please. The Monday kind is my favourite." 🙂

qa.q: On which day did Salma clap fast and snap her fingers?
qa.a: She did it on Monday.

qa.q: What did Elizabeth's stiff smile on Thursday suggest?
qa.a: It suggests the slow clap stung and she felt teased or embarrassed at being late. Her silence when she sat down fits that.

qa.q: What could Salma do differently in place of a slow clap?
qa.a: She could say a friendly greeting in words, as she promises to. That avoids a gesture that reads as sarcasm.

qa.q: How does Elizabeth see the two kinds of clapping?
qa.a: She sees the fast clap as warm praise and the slow clap as a jab. She wasn't sure of Salma's intent until she said so.

grounding: A teenager's fast clap and snap mean approval, while a slow clap reads as sarcasm, shown over three days.

subtype: Clapping and snapping in peer groups [Expressing]
passage:
"Shalini, you think a clap is always nice? Let your Chinmay Mama tell you.
When I was fifteen, I was carrying the school's football trophy onto the stage. My foot caught the step, and the trophy fell with a big clang. Silence. Then, from the back, a slow clap. Clap... clap... clap. A few boys joined. My face burned. That slow clap was mockery.
The next year, our team won again. This time, I carried the trophy perfectly, and the whole school clapped fast and loud. Same hands, same claps, but completely different meaning.
Speed and tone, Shalini. That's what tells you if it's praise or a put-down."

qa.q: What did young Chinmay drop on the stage?
qa.a: The school's football trophy.

qa.q: What was young Chinmay feeling when the slow clap started?
qa.a: He felt humiliated and embarrassed, knowing the slow clap was mockery.

qa.q: What choice inside the story turned the moment into a good memory?
qa.a: Chinmay chose to carry the trophy again the next year, and the fast, loud clapping showed real praise.

qa.q: How might the boys who slow-clapped have seen their clapping?
qa.a: They probably thought it was funny, not realising how much it hurt.

grounding: An uncle recalls how a slow sarcastic clap mocked him and a fast clap later praised him, showing tone and speed decide meaning.

subtype: Clapping and snapping in peer groups [Expressing]
passage:
At the school poetry slam, the mic had just broken, and everyone had to shout their poems over the rain on the tin roof. Arohi and her friends snapped their fingers after every good line, the club's way of cheering.
Then Divya, a shy new girl, stood up and stumbled on her second line. From the back, Sachin started a slow clap. Clap... clap... A few boys laughed.
Divya's voice shook. She looked ready to stop.
Arohi snapped her fingers fast and loud, and her friends joined in, drowning out the slow clap. "Keep going, Divya!" someone called.
Sachin's clapping trailed off.
Divya took a breath and finished her poem. The snaps were deafening.

qa.q: How did Arohi's club cheer after good lines?
qa.a: They snapped their fingers after every good line.

qa.q: What was Divya feeling when the slow clap started?
qa.a: Divya felt embarrassed and shaken, close to stopping her poem.

qa.q: What did Arohi do that turned the moment around?
qa.a: She started fast, loud snapping to cheer Divya on, drowning out the sarcastic slow clap.

qa.q: How might Sachin have seen his slow clap?
qa.a: Sachin might have thought it was funny, not noticing it was hurting Divya until the snaps drowned it out.

grounding: At a poetry slam with a broken mic, a teenager uses fast snapping to counter a sarcastic slow clap, showing tone decides meaning.

subtype: Clapping and snapping in peer groups [Expressing]
passage:
On the school basketball court in Pune, Charu missed an easy basket. Her friends on the bench clapped quickly, calling, "Next one! You've got this!"
But from the other side, Samir started a slow clap. Clap... clap... clap. His friends laughed.
Charu's cheeks went hot. She turned. "Samir, is that for real or are you making fun of me?"
Samir paused. "It was a joke."
"Didn't feel like one."
He shrugged, then said, "Okay, fair. Sorry."
Charu's friends kept clapping fast for her. On the next play, she scored, and the fast claps turned into cheers.

qa.q: What did Charu's friends call from the bench?
qa.a: "Next one! You've got this!"

qa.q: What was Charu feeling when Samir started the slow clap?
qa.a: Charu felt embarrassed and a bit angry, sensing the slow clap was mockery.

qa.q: What did Charu do that helped?
qa.a: She asked Samir directly whether the clap was real or mocking, which led him to apologise.

qa.q: How might Samir have seen his slow clap before Charu spoke up?
qa.a: Samir probably thought it was a harmless joke, not realising it hurt Charu.

grounding: On a basketball court, a teenager hears fast supportive claps from friends and a slow mocking clap, and asks about the tone.

subtype: Clapping and snapping in peer groups [Expressing]
passage:
"Okay, that verse was brilliant," Neelam said, snapping her fingers fast, snap-snap-snap. "Again!"
Raghav grinned and rapped the chorus again, and the others joined the snapping.
"Now the second verse," said Tenzin.
Raghav started, stumbled on "catastrophe", and stopped.
Clap. Clap. Clap. Neelam brought her hands together slowly, eyebrows high. The group laughed.
Raghav didn't. "Wow. Thanks."
Neelam's hands stopped. "Wait, I was joking."
"A slow clap isn't a joke when I've just messed up in front of everyone."
Neelam dropped her hands. "You're right. That was laughing at you, not with you. Sorry." She turned to the others. "He wrote that whole verse himself, you know." Then she snapped, fast and loud. "From the top. You've got it."
Raghav took a breath and nailed it.

qa.q: Which word did Raghav stumble on?
qa.a: "Catastrophe".

qa.q: Why did Neelam's hands stop?
qa.a: Neelam felt surprised and then guilty on seeing that the joking slow clap had stung Raghav.

qa.q: How did Neelam repair things?
qa.a: She admitted it was laughing at him, apologised, praised his verse to the group and switched back to fast, supportive snapping.

qa.q: What was the slow clap like for Raghav?
qa.a: Coming right after he stumbled, it felt like mockery in front of the group, and it hurt.

grounding: It shows fast snapping as approval and a slow clap as mockery among friends, with speed and tone deciding which it is.
